# EZLM beta tester guide

EZLM runs an AI model on your own computer and gives you a web address and key that other apps can use. This guide takes you from install to your first chat. If a message stops you, look it up in TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

## Install on Windows

EZLM runs on Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) and Windows 11, on regular PCs and on ARM
laptops. The installer is one file for both kinds of PC, it installs only for your Windows
account, and it does not ask for an administrator password. [1]

### Before you start

1. Check your Windows version: **Start > Settings > System > About**, under **Windows
   specifications**. EZLM needs Windows 10 version 2004 or later. [1]
2. On Windows 11, check Smart App Control: **Start > Settings > Privacy & security > Windows
   security > App & browser control > Smart App Control**. If it says **On**, read "If Smart App
   Control blocks it" below before you download. [2]
3. You do not need to install anything else first. EZLM brings its own engine and, if your PC
   lacks it, installs Microsoft's C++ runtime during setup. [3]

### Download and run the installer

1. Download **EZLM-Setup-<version>.exe** (for example EZLM-Setup-0.1.11.exe) from the beta
   download page, `https://github.com/picom-code/ezlm/releases`. [4]
2. Double-click the file. Windows may warn you first. The next two sections say what to click.
3. Setup installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\EZLM`, inside your own profile. There is no folder
   choice and no admin prompt. [1]
4. Tick **Put an EZLM icon on the desktop** if you want a shortcut there. The Start menu shortcut
   is always added. [1]
5. Press **Install**, then **Finish**. Leave **Open EZLM** ticked and EZLM opens. [1]

Running a newer installer over an older EZLM updates it in place. Your models, settings and keys
are kept because they live outside the program folder, and the installer only clears leftover
files from older builds. [5]

If EZLM is running when you start the installer, setup asks Windows to close it and reopens it
when setup finishes. [1]

### If Windows says "Windows protected your PC"

That is SmartScreen, and it appears because this beta is not code-signed yet. [2]

1. Click **More info** under the message.
2. Click **Run anyway**.

If the dialog offers no **More info** link, the file may have been blocked when it was saved.
Right-click the file, choose **Properties**, on the **General** tab tick **Unblock**, then
**OK**, and run it again.

Do not turn SmartScreen off for the whole PC. Running one file is enough.

### If Smart App Control blocks it

On Windows 11 with Smart App Control turned **On**, Windows blocks apps it does not trust, and
there is usually no **Run anyway** button. [2]

1. Open **Windows security > App & browser control > Smart App Control**.
2. If it says **On**, open **Smart App Control settings**, set it to **Off**, then run the
   installer again.
3. Turning it off is one way. Windows will not turn it back on without reinstalling Windows. If
   you want to keep it on, install EZLM on another PC.

If Smart App Control says **Evaluation**, Windows is still deciding and may allow EZLM. Try the
install and see.

### What setup does, and the one permission prompt

- It installs only for your account and adds EZLM to the Start menu. [1]
- It starts EZLM when it finishes. [1]
- On the first model setup, EZLM may install Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime, which the AI engine
  needs. Windows then shows a User Account Control prompt asking whether to allow a program to
  make changes. Click **Yes**. The file is Microsoft's redistributable, downloaded from
  Microsoft. [3]
- If you click **No** on that prompt, the engine cannot start and the first run stops at the
  engine step. Run setup again and allow it.

### If your antivirus flags EZLM

Beta builds are unsigned, so security apps may treat them as unknown. The installer, or the model
server program that EZLM downloads, can be quarantined.

What you may see:

- "EZLM's engine didn't start within 30 seconds. Your antivirus may be scanning it; try again in
  a moment." [6]
- "EZLM's engine stopped while starting. Your antivirus may have blocked it." [6]
- "The model server program was missing, so EZLM is downloading it again", followed by "EZLM's
  model server program is missing and couldn't be restored (...). If an antivirus app removed it,
  allow the folder C:\Users\<you>\.ezlm\bin in that app, then press Start server". [7]
- A download error saying a security app or company proxy is intercepting secure connections. [8]

What to do:

1. Open **Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history**. Find the EZLM
   item, open it, and choose **Allow on device** (or **Restore**).
2. Add two exclusions: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\EZLM` and `%USERPROFILE%\.ezlm\bin`. Both are
   under **Virus & threat protection > Manage settings > Exclusions > Add or remove exclusions >
   Add an exclusion > Folder**.
3. In EZLM, open **Overview** and press **Start server**, or close EZLM and open it again. [9]
4. If it happens again, press **Report a problem** and say which security app you use.

Other security suites keep their own quarantine list. Look for the same two folders there. On a
work PC behind a company proxy, ask IT to allow `github.com` and `huggingface.co`. [8]

### Check that it worked

1. The EZLM window opens. On a new install, **Overview** says "Nothing is set up yet". [10]
2. The Start menu has **EZLM**, and **Settings > Apps > Installed apps** lists EZLM. [1]
3. The folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\EZLM` contains `EZLM.exe` and an `Engine` folder with
   `ezlm.exe` inside. [1]
4. The **System** page shows your Windows version, your graphics card and the engine EZLM picked
   for it. [11]
5. **Settings > Updates** shows a line such as "EZLM 0.1.11-beta is the latest version." That
   confirms the app is running and talking to its engine. [12]
6. If you want to confirm the engine started, open `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EZLM\engine.log`. The newest
   entry starts with a date and "engine started (pid ...)". [6]

Next, set up a model. The first run is described in "First run" (a03).

### If it still will not start

- Logs are in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EZLM`: `app.log` and `engine.log`. [13]
- In EZLM, open **Logs** and press **Copy details for support**. Your keys are hidden in the
  copied text. [13]
- Press **Report a problem** and describe what happened.

## Install on macOS

EZLM for Mac comes as a disk image, `EZLM.dmg`. You drag the app into Applications and open it. The first time, macOS asks you to confirm that you trust it. This page covers that first open, what to do if EZLM says it is "running from the download", and how to check the install.

### What you need

- macOS 14 Sonoma or later. The app declares 14.0 as its minimum.[^a02-1] To check, open the Apple menu and choose **About This Mac**.
- An Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) is recommended: EZLM uses the graphics built into the chip.[^a02-2] Intel Macs work too, but the model runs on the processor and will be slower.[^a02-3]
- Free disk space for the model you pick. Models are often 2 to 60 GB.
- No separate install of the AI engine. It is inside the app.[^a02-4]

### 1. Drag EZLM into Applications

1. Download **EZLM.dmg** and double-click it. A window opens with **EZLM** and an **Applications** folder.
2. Drag **EZLM** onto **Applications**.
3. In Finder, eject **EZLM** (the eject arrow next to its name in the sidebar), then open **EZLM** from **Applications**.

The disk image is built for exactly this: the app plus a shortcut to Applications.[^a02-5] Do not run EZLM from inside the mounted disk image. If you do, macOS runs it from a temporary hidden copy, which is explained in section 3.

### 2. First open: macOS says it cannot check the app

This beta may not be notarized by Apple.[^a02-6] If your copy is not, the first time you open EZLM macOS blocks it and shows a warning that it cannot check the app for malicious software. The wording varies by macOS version. On macOS 14 and later it says **Apple could not verify “EZLM” is free of malware that may harm your Mac or your privacy.** Older versions say the app is from an **unidentified developer**. Both mean the same thing and have the same fix. If your copy is notarized, EZLM opens without this warning and you can skip to section 4.

1. In the warning, click **Done**. Do not click **Move to Trash**.
2. Open **System Settings**, then **Privacy & Security**.
3. Scroll down to the **Security** section. Next to the message about EZLM, click **Open Anyway**.
4. Confirm with your password or Touch ID.
5. macOS shows the warning again. Click **Open**.

From then on EZLM opens normally. This is Apple's standard path for an app that is not notarized, and Apple documents the same steps.[^a02-7]

If there is no **Open Anyway** button, open EZLM from Applications once more. macOS only offers the button after it has blocked a launch. If it is still missing, check that **Allow applications downloaded from** is set to **App Store and identified developers**.

On macOS 15 and later, holding Control and clicking the app no longer offers an **Open** shortcut. Use **Privacy & Security** as above.

### 3. If EZLM says it is "running from the download"

If you open EZLM straight from the disk image, or from your Downloads folder without moving it, macOS runs it from a hidden, read-only copy. This is called App Translocation. EZLM detects it and shows a gold note: **"EZLM is running from the download, so it won't be here after a restart. Drag it into Applications."** with an **Open Applications** button.[^a02-8] EZLM checks both for the hidden location and for a read-only volume.[^a02-9]

EZLM works in this state, but two things are different:

- The copy is temporary. After you quit, the next launch starts again from the original file.
- It cannot update itself in place. The updater writes the new version next to the running app, which fails on a read-only copy, so EZLM opens the disk image in Finder and asks you to drag the new copy over the old one.[^a02-10]

To fix it: quit EZLM, drag **EZLM** from the disk image or Downloads into **Applications**, choose **Replace** if asked, eject the disk image, then open EZLM from **Applications**. The gold note disappears once EZLM is running from Applications.

### 4. Check that it worked

- **Finder.** Open **Applications** and find **EZLM**. Choose **File > Get Info** to see its version.
- **The gold note is gone.** If EZLM still shows "EZLM is running from the download", it is not yet in Applications.
- **The System page.** Open EZLM and choose **System** in the list on the left. You should see **Processor**, **Graphics**, **Engine** and **Storage** lines.[^a02-11] On an Apple Silicon Mac, **Graphics** says "Built into the chip, shares system memory" and **Engine** says "Apple Metal".[^a02-12] On an Intel Mac, **Engine** says "Processor only".[^a02-13]
- **The app's data folders exist.** EZLM keeps its engine and models in `~/.ezlm`[^a02-14] and chat data in `~/Library/Application Support/EZLM`.[^a02-15] Both are created as EZLM needs them, so they may not appear until the first scan or download finishes.

If you want to confirm which copy you are running, open Terminal and run:

```sh
codesign -dv --verbose=2 /Applications/EZLM.app
```

It prints `Identifier=com.ezlm.app` for EZLM.[^a02-16] A build made on your own Mac is signed ad hoc, so it also prints `Signature=adhoc`.[^a02-17] A release build is signed with a Developer ID.[^a02-17]

### 5. If macOS says EZLM is damaged

"EZLM is damaged and can't be opened. You should move it to the Trash" usually means the copy was interrupted or macOS attached the wrong security information to it. Try these in order:

1. Move EZLM from Applications to the Trash, empty the Trash, download `EZLM.dmg` again, and drag EZLM into Applications again.
2. If it still happens, open Terminal and run:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/EZLM.app
```

Then open EZLM from Applications. This removes the "downloaded from the internet" mark that macOS puts on the app, so macOS stops checking it on launch.

### If something else goes wrong

Press **Report a problem** in EZLM, or see the troubleshooting guide. The most common macOS problems are a missing **Open Anyway** button and an app that is still running from the download; both are covered above.

## First run

The first time you open EZLM it looks at your computer, compares what it finds with the models it knows, and offers you the one it thinks suits you best. You choose whether to set that up or pick another. Nothing you type later is sent anywhere, and the first check sends nothing about your computer.

### The five checks you will see

EZLM shows a short starting screen, then a list of five checks, each with a tick when it is done. The same five lines appear on Windows and on a Mac.

- **Processor**: the name of your processor and how many threads it has.
- **System memory**: how much memory is free right now, and how much is installed. Free is the number that matters, because other apps are already using the rest.
- **Graphics**: your graphics card and how much of its memory is free, for example "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, 10.4 GB free of 12 GB". On an Apple Silicon Mac it says "Shares system memory, up to X GB for AI", because the chip uses the same memory for everything. On a computer with no supported card it says "No graphics card found, the processor will run it".
- **Disk space**: free space in the folder where models will be saved.
- **Comparing models against your memory**: how many ways EZLM found to run a model here. "Nothing fits right now" means no model fits in the memory that is free.

The numbers are a snapshot taken at that moment. Free memory and free disk space change as you use the computer, so the same screen can show different numbers an hour later.

### The screen after the scan

The next screen has two parts.

On the left is the model EZLM suggests. It shows the name, the file it will download, the download size, the speed in words per second, the context size, and whether the model works with coding agents. It also shows two bars: how much memory the model needs and how much is left over. On Windows it also shows where the model will be saved, with a **Change** button.

On the right is a switch with **Balanced**, **Smartest** and **Fastest**, and a list of up to 14 other ways to run a model on this computer. The suggested one is tagged **Recommended** and is already selected. If another program is using your graphics card, EZLM lists it here.

At the bottom of the left side are three buttons: **Set it up**, **Scan again** and **Free up memory**.

### The model it picks

The first model is the one tagged **Recommended**, at the top of the list and already selected, so **Set it up** works straight away.

To choose it, EZLM tries every model in its list with every file size, context size and memory placement that fits, then ranks the results by how smart the model is, adjusted for the quality lost in compression, as long as the speed is usable. **Balanced** is the default. **Smartest** ignores speed and **Fastest** weighs speed heavily. Changing the switch runs the comparison again and moves the selection to the new recommendation.

EZLM always leaves room for the operating system and your open apps before it plans a model. That is why the pick on a busy computer can be smaller than the same computer could run after you close a few apps. The model's download size is not limited by free disk space: if the download needs more room than you have, the screen says so in gold and lets you set it up anyway while you make room.

### How long it takes

Usually a few seconds. The checklist alone takes about two seconds on purpose, so you have time to read it, even when the check itself is instant. Three things can make it slower:

- The first start of EZLM's engine can take a few seconds, and up to 30 seconds before it reports a problem. Antivirus software scanning a new program is the usual cause.
- EZLM checks the internet for an updated model list and waits at most four seconds for it. With no connection it uses the list built into the app, so the result is the same, just from an older list.
- A slow or very full disk can slow the check of free space.

If EZLM shows "Something went wrong" with a message, press **Try again**. If it happens twice, press **Report this problem**.

### If the detection looks wrong

1. Close the apps you are not using, wait about 20 seconds, then press **Scan again**. EZLM reuses a hardware check for 20 seconds, so rescanning immediately after closing apps can show the old numbers.
2. Press **Free up memory** instead if you want EZLM to walk you through closing apps one at a time. It asks before closing anything.
3. Open **System** in the list on the left. It shows the processor, graphics, the engine EZLM chose (NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Metal, Vulkan or Processor only) and the storage folder. If the graphics line says "None found" but you have a card, update its driver, quit EZLM and open it again.
4. If the storage folder is on a small drive, change it on the first screen with **Change** next to **Saves to** (Windows), or in **Settings** (Mac). On Windows the first setup may already have put models on the drive with the most free space.
5. If memory looks lower than you expect, remember that free memory excludes what your open apps already use. Close them and scan again.
6. If the numbers are still wrong, press **Report a problem** at the bottom left, or **Copy details for support** on an error. The report includes the hardware summary and recent logs, not your keys, your files or anything you typed to a model.

## Picking or switching a model

EZLM starts with one recommended model, and you can change it at any time from **Models**. The URL, the keys and the apps you connected stay the same when you switch.[^1]

### The model list

Open **Models** to see two lists.

**On this computer** lists the models you already downloaded. Each row shows the file size, its speed and context on this machine, or "doesn't fit in free memory right now" when it needs more memory than is free.[^2] Press **Switch** to use one, or **Remove** to delete it and free the space.[^3] The model that is running has a **Running** badge and cannot be removed until you switch to another one.[^4]

**Get another model** lists the models that fit this computer, best first. The app shows up to 14 options, so on a large machine some models that fit may not be listed.[^5] The first one is marked **Recommended**.[^6] The other tags mean:

- **Running**: this is the model in use now.
- **On this computer**: the file is already downloaded, so switching needs no download.
- **Recommended**: EZLM's first choice for this computer.
- **Slow**: EZLM estimates fewer than 8 tokens a second, about 6 words a second.[^7]
- **Needs space**: there is not enough free disk for the download right now.[^8]

Each card also shows a plain description of how the model would run, for example "Dense, all 27B used per word; all on the graphics card", or "Mixture of experts, 180B total, 15B used per word; experts in system memory (44 of 60 layers), the rest on the graphics card".[^9] Below that are the file line, a **Smarts** bar, a **Speed** bar and memory bars for the graphics card and system memory.[^10] Select a card to see its own switch button. On the first-run Choose screen, the selected model also shows its file, download size, save folder, speed, context and tool support beside the list.[^11]

Above the list are **Balanced**, **Smartest** and **Fastest**. They change the order and the recommendation, not the model that is running. Balanced means "Smart, at a comfortable speed", Smartest means "Most capable model that fits, even if slow", and Fastest means "Snappy replies first".[^12] Choosing one rescans the machine and selects the new recommendation.[^13] Press **Scan again** after closing apps or plugging in a different graphics card.

### What the numbers mean

**27B** is the number of parameters in billions. A larger number usually means a more capable model that needs more memory. A mixture-of-experts model has a large total, such as 180B, but uses only a few billion parameters per word, which is why it can be bigger than the graphics card and still be quick.[^14]

**GB** on a download button or in the **Download** fact is the size of the file on disk. EZLM shows megabytes below 1 GB, one decimal below 10 GB, and whole gigabytes above that.[^15] The download can be tens of gigabytes, so a slow connection takes a while.

**Memory** on a card is not the same as the download size. It includes the model file, the context cache and the engine's working memory, so it is usually larger than the file.[^16] The bar shows how much the model needs against the memory in the machine, and how much would be left after it loads.[^17] "Not used" means the model keeps nothing in that pool.

**Context** is how much text the model can keep in mind at once, shown as 64k, 32k, 16k or 8k tokens. EZLM tries 64k first and steps down only when the larger context does not fit.[^18] Coding agents work best with 64k, and Hermes needs it.[^19]

**Smarts** compares the model with the best option on this computer, so the top model's bar is full. **Speed** is an estimate in words per second, not a measurement, and it will vary with the prompt and the machine.[^20]

The file line names the exact file, for example "UD-Q4_K_XL by unsloth", and may add "MTP speed-up" or "draft model speed-up" and "q8_0 cache".[^21] A larger file usually loses less quality, and EZLM picks the best file that fits instead of always taking the largest.[^22]

### Will it fit? Memory guidance

EZLM plans against the memory that is free now, not the memory the machine has in total. It keeps a slice back for Windows or macOS and your other apps: about 10% of free memory, with a minimum of 0.75 GB and a maximum of 2 GB. On Windows it keeps more graphics memory back, and more again on AMD and Intel cards.[^23]

If a model you want shows **Needs space**, free some disk space and scan again. You can also start the download and make room while it runs, but the download stops if the disk fills before you do.[^24]

If no model fits, close some apps and press **Scan again**.[^25] **Model mode** on the System page walks you through closing apps one at a time, and nothing closes without your OK.[^26] EZLM may also show a hint such as "Free about 6 GB to run Model Name at ~20 words/s", which tells you what closing apps would unlock.[^27]

If a file for the model is already on this computer and runs at least 85% as well as the best file, EZLM offers the downloaded file instead of a new download.[^28]

### Switching to another model

1. Open **Models**.
2. Select the model you want.
3. Press **Switch to Model Name (no download)**, **Download and switch (N GB)**, or **Resume download and switch (N GB left)**.[^29]

Your current model keeps answering while the new one downloads.[^30] EZLM stops the old server only when the new file is ready, then starts the new model, loads it and asks it a test question.[^31] If the new model fails to start, EZLM puts the previous model back.[^32] Only one change runs at a time, so the button says **Busy with another change** while another job is working.[^33]

### What happens during a download

Setup runs in stages: get the AI engine, download the model, start the server, load the model, ask it a question. The progress bar is split across those stages, and the model download is the largest part.[^34] The model download shows how much is done, how much is left, the speed in MB/s and an estimate of the time left.[^35]

Models come from Hugging Face, and the engine comes from GitHub, so the computer needs internet access for a first setup or a new model.[^36] If a security app or company proxy intercepts secure connections, the download fails with a message that names huggingface.co and github.com.[^37]

Press **Cancel** to stop the job; what was already downloaded is kept, your current model keeps running, and the next attempt resumes from there.[^38] A download that receives no data for 45 seconds is retried automatically, and a connection that keeps dropping is retried until five attempts in a row make no progress.[^39] When a model is a single file, EZLM checks the finished size and deletes a wrong-sized file, then asks you to try again.[^40]

If the disk fills during the download, EZLM stops and tells you how much space to free. Free that space and press **Set it up again**, and the download resumes where it stopped.[^41] EZLM also keeps the computer awake while a setup is running, so a long download is not interrupted by sleep.[^42]

Models are saved in `~/.ezlm/models` by default. On Windows, EZLM may choose the fixed drive with the most free space and save under `EZLM\models` there. You can change the folder under **Settings**. On Windows, the **Saves to** line on the model card shows the current folder.[^43] If space is short, EZLM removes models you are no longer using before it starts, and tells you what it removed. It never removes the model that is running unless it has to make room for a switch, and in that case it warns you that the old model would need downloading again.[^44]

## Keys and LAN mode

EZLM gives your model two things: an address and a key. The address is the same for every app that
uses it. The key is the password that proves a request is yours. This section shows where both are,
how to copy them, and what changes when you let other devices on your network use the model.

### Where the key is

Open EZLM and look at **Overview**, under **Connect with**. You get two rows, **URL** and **Key**
[1]. The key is shown masked, with its first nine characters and twelve dots, so you can recognise
it but not read it [2]. The full value is behind the **Copy** button [3].

The same two rows appear once at the end of setup, on the screen that says "Your AI is live", with
the line "Use this URL and key in any app that supports the OpenAI API." [4]

Every key EZLM makes starts with `ezlm-` and is followed by 40 random characters [5]. EZLM keeps the
key in `config.json`, inside the `.ezlm` folder in your home folder [6]. On Windows that is
`C:\Users\<you>\.ezlm\config.json`; on a Mac it is `~/.ezlm/config.json`. The file is readable only
by your own user account [7]. The key inside it is not encrypted, so anyone who can log in as you can
read it.

### Copy the key

1. Open **Overview**.
2. Find the **Key** row under **Connect with**.
3. Press **Copy**. The button says **Copied** for a moment [8].
4. Paste it into the app that asked for it.

Use **Copy** rather than reading the row: the masked text on screen does not show the full key [3].
In a terminal, `ezlm status` prints the URL, the LAN address and the full key, and `ezlm key` prints
just the key [9].

### Give each device its own key

**Keys** in the list on the left holds every key [10]. The line at the top explains the point: give
each device or app its own key, so you can revoke one without breaking the others [11].

- **New key** adds one. Type a name such as "Phone" and press **New key**; the name is only a label
  for you [12].
- The first key is the one EZLM writes into the apps it connects for you, and it is marked "used by
  connected apps" [13].
- **Rotate** replaces a key's value. Anything still using the old value stops working, and the apps
  EZLM connected are updated for you [14].
- **Revoke** deletes a key. It appears only when there is more than one key, because the server needs
  at least one [15]. If the key is the first one and apps are connected, EZLM moves those apps to the
  second key first [16].

Adding, rotating or revoking a key restarts the model server, because the list of accepted keys is
handed to the server when it starts [17]. The model reloads, which can take a minute, and a request in
flight at that moment fails. Do key work when nothing else is using the model.

### What LAN mode exposes

At the bottom of the **Keys** page, under **Network**, is a checkbox: **Let other devices on my
network use it (phones, other computers)** [18].

With it off, the model server listens on this computer only [19]. With it on, the server listens on
every network connection the computer has, and EZLM shows a **LAN URL** under the checkbox [20]. That
address is built from the computer's current network address, so it changes when you move between
networks [21]. If a device that used to work stops working, read the **LAN URL** in EZLM again and use
the new one.

LAN mode exposes the model's API and nothing else of EZLM. EZLM's own window and chat page listen on
this computer only [22], so another device gets the model, not your chat history or your files.

The key still applies. EZLM starts the model server with the key list, and the server refuses a
request that does not carry one of those keys [23]. A device on your network needs both the LAN URL
and a key.

One model serves everyone: the server runs with a single request slot, so a long request from a phone
makes your own request wait [24]. Turn the checkbox off when you are done.

The choice is remembered. It survives a restart and a model switch, so you set it once [25].

### The security trade-off in plain words

Off is the safe default. Only programs on your computer can reach the model, and nothing goes over the
network.

On means any device on the same network can reach the model if it has the key. The key is the only
lock, and the address is easy to guess on a home network. Treat the key like a password to your model:
do not paste it into a group chat or a public page.

The connection is plain HTTP, not HTTPS [26]. Nothing encrypts the traffic between your phone and your
computer, so anyone who can watch that network can read the key and the prompts. That is fine on a home
or office network you trust. On a cafe, hotel or airport network, someone else on the same network can
read it, and can then use your model.

Practical rules:

- Give each device its own key, so you can revoke one without touching the others.
- Turn LAN off when you are not using it. It is one checkbox.
- On a public network, leave it off.

### If another device cannot connect

- Use the **LAN URL**, not the address on the **Overview** page. `127.0.0.1` means "this computer" to
  whatever device opens it, so on a phone it points at the phone [27].
- An "unauthorized" or 401 answer means the key is missing, wrong or revoked. Copy it again from
  **Keys**.
- If the address does not open at all, check the checkbox is still on, then read the **LAN URL** again.
  The address may have changed.
- The first connection from another device may make Windows ask whether the model server can use the
  network. Allow it. EZLM does not create a firewall rule itself [28].
- Turning the checkbox on or off restarts the server. Wait for the model to finish loading before you
  test from the other device.

## Connecting OpenCode, Hermes and DeepSeek Harness

EZLM can put your model inside three apps:

- **OpenCode** is a coding agent that works in a terminal window.
- **Hermes** is a personal agent with tools and memory, also in a terminal.
- **DeepSeek Harness** is DeepSeek's agent harness, which runs in your browser.

You do not have to copy anything. Press **Connect**, and EZLM installs the app if it is missing, adds itself as a provider, and sends one real question to check that the app gets an answer. After that, **Open** starts the app already using your model.

### The one-click way

1. Make sure your model is running. On **Overview** the status should say **Ready** ("Waiting for requests from your apps"). If it says **The server is stopped**, press **Start server** and wait until it says **Ready** again. Connect checks that the app gets an answer, so it stays greyed out until the model is live.
2. Open **Connect** in the list on the left.
3. Click the tile of each app you want. A tile can be picked only when your model can use tools; Hermes also needs a model with a 64K context, and its tile cannot be picked when the model cannot have one.
4. Leave **Make it the default model in those apps** ticked unless you already use another model in that app and want to keep it. With the box ticked, EZLM's model becomes the app's own default, so it is used when you start the app yourself. Unticked, EZLM leaves that default alone; the **Open** buttons still open the app with EZLM's model.
5. Press the button that names your choice, for example **Connect OpenCode**. The first time, EZLM may download and install the app, which can take a few minutes.
6. Watch the tile. While EZLM works it shows what it is doing; when it finishes it says **✓ Connected and answering**. If it fails, the tile shows the reason, with **Show details** (the connection log) and **Report a problem**.
7. Press **Open OpenCode**, **Open Hermes** or **Open DeepSeek Harness (browser)** on Overview under **Use it**. The app opens in a new terminal window or in your browser, in the folder `EZLM Workspace` in your home folder, so a coding agent works on files there rather than across your whole home folder.

The check is a real conversation: EZLM asks the app to read a small file with its own file tool. A model that cannot use tools cannot be connected to these apps, and the tile says so; pick a model marked **Tools**, or use **Chat**.

### The URL and key, when an app asks for them

Most testers never need these, because Connect writes them into the app. When an app's own settings ask, use exactly what EZLM shows:

| Field | What to use |
|---|---|
| URL / Base URL | The **URL** row under **Connect with** on Overview. It looks like `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`. Press its **Copy** button rather than retyping it. |
| API key | The **Key** row beside it. The screen shows only the first nine characters and dots; press its **Copy** button to get the whole key. |
| Model | The entry EZLM added: **EZLM (local)** in OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness, provider **ezlm** in Hermes (its command-line name is **custom:ezlm**). The model's name ends in ** (EZLM)**. Do not type a model name by hand. |

Where to find them:

- **Overview > Connect with** shows the URL and the key used by connected apps, each with a Copy button.
- **Keys** in the left list shows every key. The first one is marked **used by connected apps**; the others are for phones, other computers and scripts.
- The last screen of the first-run wizard shows the same URL and key.

If you turned on **Let other devices on my network use it** on the Keys page, the Keys page also shows a **LAN URL**. On a phone or another computer use the LAN URL, not `127.0.0.1`: `127.0.0.1` always means "this computer". The LAN URL only works while EZLM is running on the machine that hosts the model.

The key is a password. Anyone who has it can use your model while EZLM is running. Do not paste it into a chat, a screenshot or a shared file. If it leaks, open **Keys**, press **Revoke** on that key, and give the app a new one.

### What EZLM writes, so you can find it later

| App | What appears in the app | Where EZLM writes it |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | Provider **EZLM (local)**; model **<your model> (EZLM)** | `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc` in `~/.config/opencode` (on Windows too, not `%APPDATA%`), plus `ezlm.key` beside it. The key is referenced as `{file:...}`, so it never sits inside the config file. `EZLM Workspace/opencode.json` picks the model for the terminal EZLM opens. |
| Hermes | Provider **ezlm** (the command line calls it **custom:ezlm**); model **<your model> (EZLM)** | `config.yaml` under `~/.hermes` (Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`), or the profile `HERMES_HOME` names. Hermes stores the key in that file as `api_key`. |
| DeepSeek Harness | Provider **EZLM (local)**; model **<your model> (EZLM)** | One `cordis.patch.yml` in each profile under `~/.dsh` (`profiles/headless`, `profiles/web`, and `profiles/desktop` if it exists), plus the key in `~/.dsh/.env` as `EZLM_API_KEY`. |

You can read these files, but do not hand-edit EZLM's own entry: EZLM replaces it the next time it connects or updates that app. Put your own settings elsewhere in the file, and they are kept.

### After you change something

You do not need to reconnect after the usual changes. When you switch model, change the port, rotate a key or add a key, EZLM updates every app it connected. If an app's tile says **Points at an old address or key: EZLM fixes it when you open it**, just press its **Open** button: EZLM rewrites the app's settings and checks them before opening. If that does not clear it, press **Connect** for that app again.

### If EZLM's model does not show up

Connect adds the model but, with **Make it the default model in those apps** unticked, leaves the app's own default alone. That only matters when you start the app yourself, without EZLM's **Open** button: it then opens with its previous model. To switch it:

- **OpenCode:** open its model list and choose the provider **EZLM (local)**, then the model ending in ** (EZLM)**. OpenCode 2.x keeps this choice per project, so make it once in `EZLM Workspace`.
- **Hermes:** choose the provider **ezlm** (shown as **custom:ezlm** on the command line) and the model ending in ** (EZLM)** in its model list, or start it with `--provider custom:ezlm -m <model id>`.
- **DeepSeek Harness:** open its model settings and choose **EZLM (local)**, then the model ending in ** (EZLM)**.

The model id is the short name in the app's config, for example `qwen3.8-27b`; it is also the id the app's own model list shows.

### Common mistakes

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Connect** is greyed out, or "Start your server first: connecting checks that the app gets an answer." | The model is not running, and Connect sends a real question to test it. | Press **Start server** on Overview and wait until the status says **Ready**. |
| The app answers "Incorrect API key" or 401. | The key was retyped from the dots on screen, or an old key was revoked. | Press **Copy** next to the Key row on Overview and paste it again. If you revoked the key, connect the app again so EZLM writes the new one. |
| The app answers "model not found" or lists no EZLM model. | The model name was typed by hand, or the app is pointed at a different EZLM model. | Choose the **EZLM (local)** entry, or press **Connect** again to have EZLM rewrite it. |
| The app cannot reach the URL, or gets a 404. | The URL was pasted without `/v1`, or the port changed after EZLM moved the server. | Copy the **URL** row again; it always includes `/v1` and the current port. |
| A phone or another computer cannot connect. | `127.0.0.1` means "this computer", so on another device it points at that device. | Turn on **Let other devices on my network use it** and use the **LAN URL** shown on the Keys page. |
| Hermes says it needs a 64K context. | Hermes refuses models with less than 64,000 tokens of context. | Press **Connect again** and EZLM gives the model the extra room (it may run slower), or pick a smaller model. |
| Hermes's tile is faded and cannot be picked. | Your model cannot reach 64K on this computer at all. | Press **Pick a smaller model**, then connect Hermes. |
| OpenCode says its history is from a newer version, its window cannot start, or it does not know a flag. | The OpenCode on your computer is older than the one EZLM tested. | Press **Connect**; EZLM installs and uses its own tested copy (2.2.5). |
| DeepSeek Harness opens a page that says "dsh web authentication required". | The browser page was opened without the one-time sign-in link `dsh web` prints, usually by visiting the address by hand. | Press **Open DeepSeek Harness (browser)** again, or reopen the link the terminal window printed. |
| DeepSeek Harness says another program is using its port. | Something else is listening on port 3080. | Close the other program, then open DeepSeek Harness again. |
| DeepSeek Harness says **EBADENGINE** or that Node.js is too old. | Its Node.js is older than 22.19.0. | Press **Connect**; EZLM installs its own Node.js and uses that. |
| OpenCode stops sending a key after you cleaned up your config folder. | `ezlm.key` was deleted; OpenCode 2.x then sends no key at all, without an error. | Press **Connect** to write the key file again. |
| You edited EZLM's entry in an app's config and your change disappeared. | EZLM owns that entry and rewrites it on every connect, model switch and key change. | Keep your own settings outside EZLM's entry; press **Connect** after changing anything EZLM manages. |

### If you would rather not use the buttons

The command line does the same work: `ezlm connect opencode hermes dsh` connects the apps you name, and adding `--default` makes EZLM's model the default in them. `ezlm doctor apps` prints each app's state, its config file, its last check and a quick launch check, without opening anything.

## Chat

**Chat** in the list on the left is EZLM's own chat window. It talks to the model running on this computer, with the address and key already filled in, so there is nothing to set up. Nothing you type leaves the machine.

Chat needs your model running. If it is stopped you see **Your model is stopped.** with a **Start server** button; if no model is set up yet you see **Set up a model first: pick one in Models.** (macOS `ChatView.swift:186-199`, Windows `Chat.cs:537-541`). Start the server, then type in the box at the bottom.

### The line at the top

- The dot and word show what your model is doing: **live**, **loading**, **stopped**, **not set up**, **writing**, or **busy with another app** when OpenCode, Hermes or a script is using it (macOS `ChatView.swift:62-71`, Windows `Chat.cs:504-541`).
- **chat size** is how much of the model's memory this conversation has used, as a bar and as a number like `2.1k / 32k` (macOS `ChatView.swift:77-82`).
- **tokens/s** is the answer speed.
- **thinking on / thinking off** lets a thinking model work through the question before it answers. Off sends you straight to the answer (macOS `ChatModel.swift:389`, Windows `Chat.cs:123`).
- **✦ memory** opens what the chat remembers about you (see below).
- **Model** switches to another model you have installed. The chat carries on, and each answer is labelled with the model that wrote it (macOS `ChatView.swift:91-102`, `ChatModel.swift:28`). The switch restarts the server, so wait for it to say **live** again.
- **History** reopens an earlier chat, copies the current one, deletes one or all of them, or opens llama.cpp's own chat page in your browser (macOS `ChatView.swift:103-115`, Windows `Chat.cs:1153-1188`).
- **New chat** starts an empty conversation. It also works with `Command+N` on a Mac and `Ctrl+N` on Windows.

### Asking something

Type in the box and press Return (Enter on Windows) to send. Option+Return adds a new line on a Mac. While an answer is arriving, **Stop** or the Esc key ends it and keeps what was written so far (macOS `ChatView.swift:217-247`, Windows `Chat.cs:291-316`).

The up arrow brings back your last message, with any files, so you can change it and send again. Type `/` to see the commands, and Tab completes one:

- `/remember` and a fact saves something about you for later chats.
- `/forget` and a word removes what it remembers that mentions it.
- `/memory` opens the memory list.
- `/new` starts a new chat.
- `/help` lists them.

Commands are handled by EZLM and never sent to the model (macOS `ChatModel.swift:393-421`, Windows `Chat.cs:750-777`). If you type a slash and no command matches, the message goes to the model as ordinary text.

On an empty chat EZLM offers three example questions. Click one to try it (macOS `ChatModel.swift:83-87`, `ChatView.swift:131-140`).

### Reading the answer

Answers stream in a few words at a time and are drawn as formatted text: headings, lists, quotes, tables, links, and code blocks with their own **Copy** button (Windows `Markdown.cs:12-99`). Under each finished answer you get:

- **Copy** puts the answer on the clipboard.
- **Listen** reads it aloud with the computer's own voice. Press it again to stop (macOS `ChatModel.swift:599-617`, Windows `Chat.cs:951-985`). If Windows has no voice installed, EZLM says so and tells you where to add one.
- **Retry** asks the same question again and replaces the old answer.
- **Continue** appears when the answer hit the model's limit or you stopped it. It sends the end of the answer back and asks the model to go on (macOS `ChatView.swift:301-304`, `ChatModel.swift:575-578`).
- A line with the speed, the number of tokens, and whether messages were left out.

With **thinking on**, the answer first shows its thinking live, then folds it into a **thought for 12s** line you can open. A very long think offers **Answer without thinking** after 40 seconds (macOS `ChatView.swift:329-347`).

### Files

Press **+ file** or drag a text file onto the page. The file is sent with your next question and shown as a tag with its size in tokens (macOS `ChatView.swift:36-44`, `ChatModel.swift:469-497`).

- Text files only: plain text, code, CSV, Markdown, and similar. PDF and Word files are not read yet, and EZLM says to copy their text in instead.
- A file over 2 MB is refused with a note to copy in the part you need.
- A file too large for the model's memory is refused before it is attached, with the token count it would need.
- Older turns make way for a file, but the file and the question have to fit on their own.

### What it remembers

The chat keeps a short list of facts about you, in `memory.md` next to its saved chats, and sends them to the model at the start of each new chat as background, not as instructions (macOS `ChatData.swift:114-241`, Windows `Memory.cs`).

- After a chat goes quiet for about 8 seconds, the model is asked once for lasting facts you mentioned. New ones appear under the answer as **✦ remembered** with a **forget** button (macOS `ChatModel.swift:425-457`, Windows `Chat.cs:784-820`).
- **✦ memory** shows every fact, lets you delete one, add one, write your own instructions ("keep answers short"), and turn the whole thing off.
- Facts are kept under 1,500 characters, about 400 tokens. When it is full EZLM says **Memory is full: remove something in Memory first.**
- Things that look like an instruction or a secret are not saved, for example "ignore previous instructions", a password, or a card number (macOS `ChatData.swift:186-210`).

### Saved chats

Every chat is saved on this computer as you go, one file per conversation, so closing EZLM does not lose it. On Windows they are in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EZLM\chats`; on a Mac in `~/Library/Application Support/EZLM/chats` (macOS `ChatData.swift:3-15,49`, Windows `ChatStore.cs:43`). The first time you open Chat, the most recent chat from the past week comes back (macOS `ChatModel.swift:125-131`, Windows `Chat.cs:93-97`). **History** lists the last 15, and **Copy this chat** copies the whole conversation as text.

### Limits to know about

- One conversation at a time. There are no folders, no search, and no editing an earlier question. **Retry** only redoes the last one.
- The model reads a fixed amount of text at once. When a chat gets near that, EZLM leaves out the oldest messages and shows **This chat has nearly filled the model's memory, so its oldest messages are left out from here. New chat starts fresh.** (macOS `ChatView.swift:200-202`, Windows `Chat.cs:538`). Answers then start to forget the beginning of the conversation.
- An answer can stop at the model's own limit. Use **Continue** to carry on, or ask for something shorter.
- Text only. There is no picture, audio or PDF input, and no web browsing: the model answers from what it was trained on and what you paste in.
- If the whole question and file still do not fit, EZLM says **That's more than the model can read at once, even with older messages left out. Try a shorter message or file.**
- Quitting EZLM in the middle of an answer stops it there. What was written so far is kept (macOS `AppModel.swift:195`, Windows `Chat.cs:533`).
- Chat is one app using the model. Another app using it at the same time shares the same server, so answers can be slower, and the top line says **busy with another app**.
- The key is filled in for you here. Other apps still need the URL and key from **Connect** or **Keys**.

### If an answer fails

Each of these appears in place of the answer, and asking again usually clears it:

- **Your model is still loading. Try again in a moment.** The server is starting.
- **Couldn't reach your model. It may have stopped: check Overview.** Start the server again.
- **Your model stopped in the middle of answering. Check Overview, then ask again.**
- **It didn't answer. Try asking again.** and **It thought about it but didn't write an answer. Try asking again.** The model returned nothing.
- **The server didn't accept EZLM's key. Restart EZLM; if it keeps happening, report a problem.**
- **Something went wrong:** followed by the system's own words.

The full list, with the cause of each, is in TROUBLESHOOTING.

## Updating and uninstalling EZLM

### Updating

EZLM checks for a new version when it opens and keeps the answer for an hour.[^1] To check by hand, open **Settings**, find **Updates**, and press **Check for updates**.[^2] When a new version is out, EZLM shows its version number, the download size, and an **Update to x.y.z** button.[^3] On Windows, EZLM tells you your model keeps running while EZLM restarts itself.[^3] On both platforms EZLM opens again by itself when the update is finished.[^4]

What happens when you press the button:

1. EZLM downloads the installer to a temporary folder on your computer.[^5]
2. It checks the file against the fingerprint (SHA-256) that GitHub publishes for it. If they differ, EZLM deletes the file and installs nothing.[^6]
3. On **Windows**, EZLM closes its own helper processes, starts the downloaded installer silently, and quits. The installer replaces the app's files and opens EZLM again.[^7] If the installer stops early, it opens the copy of EZLM that is already installed, so you are not left without the app.[^8]
4. On a **Mac**, EZLM mounts the disk image, checks that it contains EZLM, copies the new version next to the old one, swaps them, and opens the new one.[^9] If it cannot write to Applications, it opens the disk image and asks you to drag EZLM into Applications yourself.[^10]

If you quit during the download, the update stops and you can start it again from Settings.[^11] A second try reuses a complete downloaded file instead of fetching it again.[^12]

If EZLM was opened straight from the disk image or from Downloads, macOS runs it from a temporary read-only copy. EZLM shows a note asking you to drag it into Applications, because it cannot replace itself there.[^13] Move it to Applications first, then update.

If checking fails, Settings says "couldn't reach GitHub to check for updates" or "checking for updates failed (…)".[^14] Your installed version keeps working, so try again later. After an update, Settings shows the new version number, and your models and chats are unchanged.[^15]

### Uninstalling on Windows

You can remove EZLM in either of two ways:

- **Settings > Apps > Installed apps > EZLM > Uninstall.** This removes the app, its shortcuts and its startup entry.[^16]
- **Inside EZLM: System > Remove models and settings.** This stops the model and deletes the models, settings and keys, but leaves the app installed.[^17]

The uninstaller asks "Also delete the AI models EZLM downloaded, and its settings and keys?" and the default answer is **No**.[^18]

- **Yes** stops the model server, removes the startup entry, deletes the models (including models on another drive) and deletes the data folder.[^19]
- **No** stops the model server and keeps the data, and does not record it as your choice, so a reinstall starts the model again.[^20]

What is left behind on Windows:

- If you answered **No**, `%USERPROFILE%\.ezlm` stays. It holds the models, the settings, your API keys, the logs and the downloaded engine.[^21] A later reinstall finds the models and does not download them again.[^22]
- In both cases, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EZLM` stays. It holds chat history, memory and the app's own logs, and neither uninstall path deletes it.[^23] Delete the folder by hand if you want it gone.
- In both cases, the downloaded installer stays in `%TEMP%\EZLM-update` until Windows clears its temporary files.[^5] It is safe to delete.
- The startup entry is removed either way, so EZLM does not come back at sign-in.[^24]
- If you used the in-app button, EZLM is still open and scans again, which recreates an empty `%USERPROFILE%\.ezlm` folder. An empty folder is expected.[^32]

### Uninstalling on Mac

1. In EZLM, open **System**, press **Remove models and settings**, then **Remove everything**.[^25]
2. Drag **EZLM** from Applications to the Trash.[^26]

The button stops the model, removes the login item, and deletes the models, the settings and the keys.[^27]

What is left behind on a Mac:

- `~/Library/Application Support/EZLM` stays. It holds chat history and memory, because the uninstall deletes only `~/.ezlm` and the model folders.[^28] Delete the folder by hand.
- The login item `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.ezlm.server.plist` is removed by the button.[^29] If you drag the app to the Trash without pressing the button first, the file stays and points at an app that is no longer there, so delete it by hand.
- The disk image in Downloads, and the temporary copy in `$TMPDIR/EZLM-update`, stay until you or macOS deletes them.[^30]
- If you skip step 1, `~/.ezlm` stays with the models, settings and keys, and a reinstall finds the models again.[^31]
- After the button, EZLM is still open and scans again, which recreates an empty `~/.ezlm` folder. An empty folder is expected, and you can delete it once EZLM is closed.[^32]

### Reinstalling later

On both platforms, a reinstall that keeps the data folder skips the model download and starts the model at sign-in again.[^22] To start from scratch instead, answer **Yes** on Windows, or press **Remove models and settings** on a Mac before trashing the app, and then reinstall.
